title: Incremental decomm plan and customer-ready kit for retiring legacy model variants
creator: Marco Diaz
description: Purpose: produce an executable, incremental decommissioning plan to retire two legacy model variants (rwd-llm-legacy and rwd-llm-legacy-opt) and onboard customers to the v2 family with minimal service disruption. Deliverables: customer-ready migration kit (guided migration doc, automated compatibility shim, SDK migration helpers, sample prompts), coordinated release notes and comms calendar, rollback/playback plan, and telemetry gating for GA cutover. This ticket covers PM coordination, release notes templates, cross-team GTM tasks, and success criteria so that engineering, design, support, and GtM can run a single unified launch.
acceptance_criteria: Customer migration kit published in Confluence + public docs link with step-by-step migration guide
Automated compatibility shim merged (ENG PR) and validated on staging with synthetic workload (latency + correctness thresholds met)
Release notes and GTM comms calendar drafted and reviewed by legal/PR/support
Support playbook and canned responses staged in Zendesk/HelpCenter
Rollback and fallback policies documented and verified with a fire-drill in staging
Telemetry dashboards show migration KPIs (migration rate, error rate, latency delta) and alert thresholds configured

risks: Customers using undocumented prompt hacks may see behavior regressions — mitigation: compatibility shim + feature flag rollout + prompt audit
Latency delta for migrated workloads exceeding SLA in tail-percentiles — mitigation: staged pilots and performance gating for GA
Insufficient support capacity during migration window — mitigation: schedule overlap with on-call support and preparedness runbook
Automated migration tools could mis-map model parameters for some customers — mitigation: provide manual override steps in playbook and quick rollback
Documentation or release notes miscommunication leading to customer confusion — mitigation: review loop with support and developer advocates
